# Fixture provenance: rows that share a GUID (#1195)

Every book here is invented, with round figures and plain names: no fixture is a Tally read of any real assessee.

## What these fixtures establish, and what they do not

The reference changed, at its commit `976ba9dd`, how four modules cite the vouchers behind a row. Before it, `cash_payments_40a3` and `high_value_register` keyed a row's vouchers by GUID alone, so two vouchers sharing a GUID (a blank GUID, or one GUID repeated) in one row were cited as one voucher; and `counter_cheques_40a3` gave two over-limit lines with the same date, GUID and ledger the same row id, so the reference refused the whole test with a duplicate figure id. Now a row keys its vouchers by GUID and label (the evidence ref's id stays the GUID), `entity_269st_gap` projects back to one unlabelled ref per distinct GUID so its output does not move, and `counter_cheques_40a3` adds an ordinal suffix only where today's id would repeat. The figure values, every id that was unique before and every other finding are unchanged: the 130 goldens already pinned regenerate byte-identical at `976ba9dd` (checked 5 Oct 2026).

- `edge-books/cp_shared_guid_row.json` (`cash_payments_40a3`): two blank-GUID cash payments to one payee on one day, told apart by their numbers (an s.40A(3) row and an s.269ST payment-leg party row); two blank-GUID receipts from one party on one day; two blank-GUID walk-in sales and two blank-GUID cash purchases on one day (the unnamed rows of each leg); one GUID on two payments to one payee on one day; two blank-GUID payments with no number (identical refs, so cited once); a unique GUID with two lines to one payee (cited once); two blank-GUID cash drawings to a capital ledger (an excluded row, cited in its excluded total). 32 figures, 9 findings.
- `edge-books/hvr_shared_guid_row.json` (`high_value_register`): two blank-GUID receipts from one party on one day (a party-day row; at `976ba9dd` the voucher-grain row keyed by GUID and stayed one row); two blank-GUID cash purchases on one day; two blank-GUID receipts on two days sharing a reference (a single-transaction row), beside a blank-GUID receipt with no reference (at `976ba9dd` the unreferenced count was of distinct GUIDs and did not move) and a unique-GUID one. 52 figures, 6 findings. Since #1243 (below) the voucher grain and the unreferenced count are per voucher: its golden was regenerated, its book's comment says so, and both byte rows are updated in place.
- `edge-books/ep_shared_guid_row.json` (`entity_269st_gap`): two blank-GUID receipts on one ledger and a unique-GUID receipt on a second ledger with the same PAN, on one day. The gap row still cites one unlabelled ref per distinct GUID; at the reference's previous commit the golden is byte-identical. 7 figures, 1 finding.
- `edge-books/cc_repeat_row.json` (`counter_cheques_40a3`): one voucher with two over-limit lines to one expense ledger, and two blank-GUID over-limit payments to that ledger on one day; each takes `_1`, `_2` in the rows' sort order, and a unique-GUID payment on the same day and a line on another ledger keep today's id. At the reference's previous commit the reference refuses this book (`duplicate figure id`), so it has no pristine golden. 24 figures, 6 findings.
- Not reached: `tds_payees` and the read-only suspects, where a shared GUID merges figure VALUES (tracked as #1243, not changed here).
- Regression fixtures only: they prove the port and the reference agree on the same book, and nothing about reading Tally. The evidence for real books is local parity on real reads, never committed.

## `high_value_register` keys a voucher by its own key (#1243)

The reference changed again, at its commit `f7240763`. `high_value_register` kept its (party, voucher) grain's rows, and every row's per-voucher shares and money lines, by GUID, and counted the vouchers with no reference as distinct GUIDs; so two vouchers sharing a GUID were one voucher in each (the grain's count, a "voucher" over the limit that no voucher reached, a cash line that differs on each voucher but cancels in the sum, a voucher with no reference hidden by one with the same GUID that has one). Each voucher now has a key of its own (its GUID where no other voucher of the population has it, else the GUID and its place among those sharing it), and the grain, the shares, the lines and the count are by that key; citations still name the GUID. A journal-transfer row id that would repeat (two blank-GUID journals, one GUID on two journals, or both lines of one journal on one party ledger, which the reference refused with a duplicate figure id) takes its place among the rows sharing it, in date and ledger order and then reading order, as a suffix `_1`, `_2`; every other id is as before. Of the 135 goldens pinned before this, only `edge.hvr_shared_guid_row.high_value_register.json` changes (six counts: the voucher grain's and the unreferenced vouchers'); the other 134 regenerate byte-identical at `f7240763` (checked 6 Oct 2026).

- `edge-books/hvr_shared_guid_voucher.json` (new): one GUID on two cash receipts from one party on one day, and on two cash payments to one party, and two blank-GUID bank receipts from one party (two vouchers each at the voucher grain, neither over the limit); two blank-GUID receipts from one party, and two with no party, whose cash line differs from the party's side on each voucher though the sums agree (each row now shows its cash line); one GUID on receipts from two parties, and a two-party voucher with a GUID of its own, none with a reference (three vouchers with no reference: the two-party voucher is one voucher in two rows); one GUID on a receipt with a reference and one without (the one without is counted); five blank-GUID receipts read out of number order (cited in label order). 61 figures, 9 findings; at `f7240763`'s parent it differs in eight counts (the voucher grain's and the unreferenced vouchers') and in the two rows that now show their cash line.
- `edge-books/hvr_journal_suffix.json` (new): four blank-GUID journals between two party ledgers, read out of date order with two on one day, beside a fifth under the threshold (not counted among those sharing an id); one GUID on two journals on one day; a journal with a GUID of its own whose two lines are on one party ledger, credit first, and another with the debit line first (the reference gives `_1` to the debit line there; added with a regenerated golden at the reference's commit `ee17d80f`, where the golden's earlier rows are unchanged and only the two new rows, their codes and the two line counts are added); a journal with a GUID of its own that keeps its ids; and one GUID on a journal over the threshold and one under it (only rows over it are counted among those sharing an id, so the one over keeps its id). 87 figures, 23 findings; at `f7240763`'s parent the reference refuses this book (`duplicate figure id`), so it has no pristine golden.

## How they were produced

At the reference engine (a private repository), commit `976ba9dd`, under Python 3.13; the three `high_value_register` goldens at its commit `ed9a29af8a4dec76baf3ea42c3425e9b0151e642` (6 Oct 2026, from an archive of its `tae/` only), where they are byte-identical to `f7240763`'s and every `high_value_register` golden already committed (four edge books and the synthetic read) regenerates byte-identical except `hvr_shared_guid_row`'s, as above. A key's place is zero-padded since the reference's `19617356`; no `high_value_register` golden moves for it:

    uv run -q --python 3.13 --with openpyxl --with xlrd --with python-docx --with jsonschema \
        --with striprtf --with pdfplumber python parity/edge_golden.py ENGINE \
        tests/fixtures/edge-books/NAME.json tests/fixtures/golden

The six books are hand-written scenarios, not generated from any data (the two #1243 books are written as data by a small generator, then read by both sides).
